size_why: One item (Healbane) and seven hero kits, zero systems, economy, map or objective changes — the 10-30 framework is untouched. The tier list moves at the bottom (Celeste C→D, Baba and Deadman Danny trimmed) but nothing about how souls are earned or where fights happen changes.
headline: The anti-heal arms race that 10-30 started gets capped: one Healbane per team is now correct, and sustain comps quietly win the patch.

meta_thesis.previous: Convert a lead into Guardians/Walkers before the comeback economy catches up, off the back of one-cycle Haunt camp clearers and late scalers who now have a farm floor.
meta_thesis.new: Same economy, same farm routes, same objective clock — but the 10-30 answer to sustain (stack Healbane across the team) is now inefficient, so heal-and-grind frontlines hold ground they previously lost and burst-pick comps lose their coverage slot.
meta_thesis.why: No systems moved, so tempo and farm logic are inherited wholesale; the only meta-wide lever is Healbane's 4-stack cap falling 82.2%→72%, which re-prices anti-heal as a single-buyer slot rather than a team tax.

winners.why: Scorn heal 1.2x→1.3x, Combo HP/kill 40→50, Burrow radius +0.5m and a stronger Sand Blast T2 slow — the patch's biggest direct kit gain, and the softer Healbane cap protects the Scorn sustain that funds it.
Dome and heal throughput were the main casualty of stacked anti-heal; the 4-stack cap cut is a direct reprieve, and his own Healbane is single-source so he loses nothing on the giving side.
Tether healing was the most exposed heal to multi-buyer Healbane and her losing matchups (Vyper, Yamato, Dynamo, Mo & Krill) took no buffs — uncontested relief.
Riposte now disarms and Pummel strips a pre-existing parry, plus T2 duration and Itani Lo Sahn T3 damage up — he wins trades he previously only stalled.
Bullet damage +8% and a faster, wider fear cone (2s→1.75s buildup, 50%→65% vertical) reward the mag-dump gun line her sustain build already runs.

losers.why: Silence, cast range, spirit amp, ult slow, ult cooldown, bounce, T1 and T2 all cut at once — a full-kit trim on a hero already sitting at C, which is a burial rather than an outlier correction.
Spirit resist scaling 0.7→0.5, melee damage -10% per boon, Brew cooldown/burn/cycle all worse and Granny Long Legs resists 30%→25% — the bruiser shell that was her identity is thinner on every axis.
Close The Deal +75%→+55%, Strix Salvo spirit scaling -8%, Chimera Mk1 heal 150→125 and 2.0→1.7 — his dive converts fewer kills and he has no sustain shell to fall back on.
His anti-heal bruiser build paired Healbane with a built-in heal cut; the 4-stack cap cut trims exactly that composition while his spirit melee core is untouched.
Softer stacked anti-heal makes the sustain archetype that already erases his hook combo (Kelvin, his worst matchup at 42%) harder to burst through, and he got nothing back.

non_obvious_calls.claim: The Healbane change is a stealth buff to dedicated healers, not a nerf to any individual buyer — single-source anti-heal is unchanged, so only coordinated double-buys lose value.
non_obvious_calls.why: 2 stacks 57.8%→54.7% and 4 stacks 82.2%→72% while one source is flat; the losers are teams treating Healbane as a coverage slot, the winners are Kelvin/Ivy/Rem/Mo & Krill.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Mo & Krill's buffs ripple across the frontline matchup chart more than his own tier suggests — Holliday, Viscous, Mirage and Yamato all list him as a losing lane.
non_obvious_calls.why: Scorn 1.2x→1.3x plus Combo 40→50 makes the lockdown frontline harder to burst for every commit-heavy diver that already struggled into him.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Apollo's Riposte buff is real but does not undo the 10-30 loss — a disarm wins trades, it does not restore channel interruption.
non_obvious_calls.why: Pommel Hit's stun became an immobilize plus parry disable on 10-30; adding disarm and parry-break sharpens his lane bullying without giving back the interrupt.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Rat King's T1 -25s banner cooldown partially reverts the 10-30 uptime cut and frees a build slot.
non_obvious_calls.why: Superior/Compress Cooldown were near-mandatory to keep the banner up; T1 now covers that, so the slot can go to damage or defence.

uncertainties: Whether teams actually stop double-buying Healbane — the doctrine change is the whole patch, and habit may hold buy rates flat for a week.
Celeste's nerf is large enough to be a burial, but she was already C-tier; whether she falls out of pick consideration entirely or just becomes a niche counterpick is unclear.
Baba's resist-scaling cut may push her to a pure cooldown-caster build rather than killing her — the KB does not tell me how much of her win rate came from the bruiser shell.
The Graves snapshot (56.5% WR / 40.9% PR vs KB 48.5% / 21%) is still unresolved and nothing in this patch touches her, so I cannot place her.
Calico: the hero analysis reads her down off Victor/Abrams sustain, but the standing reader note says she gains from tempo — I am not confident which dominates with no systems change.
what_to_watch: Healbane buys per team per game — if the double-buy rate does not fall, the patch's only meta lever did nothing.
Kelvin, Ivy and Rem win rates in the first week — the cleanest read on whether the anti-heal cap actually restored healer value.
Mo & Krill pick rate against win rate — his buffs are the largest single-hero gain and should show up as a pick-rate bump before a win-rate one.
Celeste pick rate — a C→D nerf should show as a near-total disappearance, not a dip.
Average game length — with no systems change it should stay flat; if it rises, sustain comps are stalling out the comeback clock.
